accepted.question_text: For each integer d at least 3, does there exist an infinite family of d-dimensional bounded-degree simplicial complexes that are coboundary expanders with F2 coefficients? Equivalently, can one construct higher-dimensional analogues of expander graphs whose vertex degrees stay uniformly bounded while their d-dimensional F2-coboundary Cheeger constants remain uniformly bounded away from zero?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded-degree F2 coboundary expanders in dimensions >= 3

evidence.quote: Problem 1.3. For d ≥ 2, are there families of d-dimensional bounded degree F2-coboundary expanders?
In Section 5, we provide a solution to Problem 1.3 for the d = 2 case (it remains open for d ≥ 3).

accepted.question_text: Let G be a simple p-adic Lie group of rank d at least 3, let B be its associated Bruhat-Tits building, and let Γ be a lattice in G. When the residue characteristic p is sufficiently large as a function of d, must the quotient complex Γ\B have positive first cocycle Cheeger constant with permutation coefficients? In other words, is h_1(Γ\B, Sym) always strictly positive in this high-rank p-adic setting?
accepted.context_brief: Permutation-coefficient cocycle expansion for p-adic lattices

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.1. Let G be simple p-adic Lie group of rank d ≥ 3, and p ≥ p(d) ≫ 0. Then, for any lattice Γ of G, (6.1) h1(Γ\B, Sym) > 0, where B is the Bruat–Tits building associated with G.
Unfortunately, we are currently not able to prove the above.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely presented group that is not sofic? Equivalently, is there a finitely presented group for which no sequence of approximate homomorphisms into finite symmetric groups can simultaneously asymptotically satisfy all defining relations while keeping every nontrivial word uniformly far from the identity permutation?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3 (Gromov [Gro99], Weiss [Wei00]). Are there non-sofic groups?
The existence of non-sofic groups is a long standing problem, and many examples of groups have been suggested as candidates for being non-sofic.

accepted.question_text: Is there an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes of uniformly bounded degree for which both the 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional coboundary Cheeger constants with permutation coefficients are uniformly bounded below by a positive constant? That is, can one build bounded-degree complexes Xm such that h_0^B(Xm, Sym) and h_1^B(Xm, Sym) are each at least some fixed λ > 0 for all m?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded coboundary expanders with permutation coefficients

evidence.quote: Problem 6.5 (Bounded coboundary expanders in permutations). Is there such a family for which ∀m ∈ N : hB0 (Xm, Sym), hB1 (Xm, Sym) ≥ λ, for some λ > 0 independent of m?

accepted.question_text: Is there an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes of uniformly bounded degree that are simultaneously cocycle expanders in dimensions 0 and 1 with permutation coefficients and also have uniformly large 1-dimensional cosystoles with permutation coefficients? Concretely, can one find bounded-degree complexes Xm for which h_0(Xm, Sym), h_1(Xm, Sym), and CoSyst_1(Xm, Sym) are all at least a fixed λ > 0 independent of m?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded cocycle expanders with large permutation cosystoles

evidence.quote: Problem 6.6 (Bounded cocycle expanders with large cosystoles in permutations). Is there such a family for which ∀m ∈ N : h0(Xm, Sym), h1(Xm, Sym), CoSyst1(Xm, Sym) ≥ λ, where λ > 0 is independent of m?
Solving Problem 6.6 will be the exact Sym analogue of [KKL16] with F2 coefficients.

accepted.question_text: For the groups SL_n(F_p), and more generally for finite simple groups of Lie type, is there a uniform positive lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations for the expansive Steinberg presentations, at least when n is fixed and p tends to infinity? Conversely, do the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations for the much shorter Guralnick-Kantor-Kassabov-Lubotzky presentations necessarily tend to zero when either n or p tends to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Stability tradeoff for Steinberg versus GKKL presentations

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.7. There is a uniform lower bound on the cocycle Cheeger constant in permutations of the Steinberg presentations, at least when fixing n and tending p to ∞. On the contrary, the cocycle Cheeger constants in permutations of the GKKL presentations tend to zero when either n or p tending to ∞.

accepted.question_text: Can one find a family of finite groups G with presentations G ≅ <S|R> that are simultaneously short and efficiently stable in permutations, in the sense that the numbers of generators and relations and the lengths of the relations are all polylogarithmic in |G|, while the homomorphism stability rate satisfies ρ(ε) = polyloglog(|G|) · ε^c for some universal exponent c > 0?
accepted.context_brief: Efficient stability in permutations for short presentations

evidence.quote: Problem 6.9 (Efficient stability in permutations). Find a family of finite groups {G}, with presentations G ∼= hS|Ri, such that: • The presentation is (somewhat) short: |S|, |R| = polylog(|G|) ∀r ∈ R : |r| = polylog(|G|). • The stability rate is good: hS|Ri is ρ-stable, and ρ(ε) = polyloglog(|G|) · ε^c for some c > 0 independent of |G|.
The motivation for this parameter setting is that it allows for randomness generation in certain contexts.

accepted.question_text: Given a binary linear code Ker(A) defined by a matrix A in M_{m×n}(F2), consider the associated presentation of an elementary abelian 2-group with generators x_i, order-two relations x_i^2, commutation relations x_i x_j x_i^{-1} x_j^{-1}, and the linear relations induced by the rows of A. What can be proved about the homomorphism stability rate of this presentation when approximate homomorphisms are allowed to take values in arbitrary symmetric groups Sym(n), rather than being restricted to Sym(2)? In particular, for structured code families such as Reed-Muller codes or recently constructed good locally testable codes, do these presentations admit strong stability rates with permutation coefficients?
accepted.context_brief: Locally testable codes with permutation coefficients

evidence.quote: Problem 6.11 (Locally testable codes with permutation coefficients). Given a matrix A ∈ Mm×n(F2), one can define the following presentation of Fk2, where k = n − rank(A) ... What about the case where the inputs are not restricted to be with range Sym(2), but any Sym(n)? Namely, what can be said about the homomorphism stability rate of the above presentation for a given code?

For the Hadamard code the resulting presentation is essentially the multiplication table of Fk2, and is thus stable but expansive. What about more reasonably sized codes, such as Reed–Muller codes? Or, the recently constructed good locally testable codes [DEL+22,PK22]?
